documents.title: Stereotactic Radiosurgery Treatment Summary
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
RADIOSURGERY TREATMENT SUMMARY (received 01/24/2023)
Treatment date: 01/18/2023

Diagnosis: right vestibular schwannoma, 2.0 cm.
Technique: single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery with a planning MRI fused to CT the same morning. Marginal dose 12 Gy.
Course: treatment delivered without interruption. No nausea, headache or new deficit afterward. Discharged home the same day with a companion.

Post-treatment: may notice temporary fatigue or a mild increase in tinnitus over the next weeks. Follow-up MRI at 6 months, then yearly. Call for new facial weakness, imbalance or severe headache.

Allergies: NKDA. HAE: no airway manipulation required; icatibant available.

Radiation Oncology / Neurotology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks after radiosurgery for the R vestibular schwannoma. Treatment summary reviewed. Tired for about a week afterward, back to normal now, working full days. Hearing on the R the same as before, ringing the same. R face: still a slight droop at the corner of the mouth when she smiles, not worse. No headache, dizziness or imbalance.
HAE: no attacks since last year's hand episode. BP fine at home.

Exam: BP as recorded. Mild R lower facial droop, eye closure full. Gait steady, tandem okay. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P
1. Vestibular schwannoma s/p SRS 1/2023 - stable symptoms; 6-month MRI in July per skull base team.
2. HTN - controlled on HCTZ. BMP.
3. HAE - quiet.
Physical in June.

documents.body: Hi, I have a cleaning at the dentist in two weeks. Do I need that pre-treatment the allergy doctor talked about? Thanks, Jen

documents.title: RE: Dentist question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jen, a routine cleaning is not what they meant. The C1 inhibitor pre-treatment is for extractions, implants or other bigger dental procedures, and for surgery. If the dentist plans anything more than a cleaning, call the allergy office first. Bring your icatibant with you to the appointment either way. See you June 8.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 48F.

Interval since March: no new problems. Hearing R ear unchanged, tinnitus the same, face unchanged. MRI follow-up scheduled for July. No HAE attacks in 2023 so far; icatibant syringes in date. Neck occasionally stiff, no arm symptoms. Home BP 120s/high 70s.

Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; icatibant 30 mg SC as needed (allergy). NKDA.
FH: mother C1-INH deficiency; father HTN, stroke at 60; maternal uncle died young of throat swelling.
Social: never smoker, a drink or two a month, office administrator.
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Well appearing. Mild R lower facial droop, unchanged. Hearing reduced R to whisper. Neck supple. Heart: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear. Breasts: no masses or skin changes, axillae clear. Abdomen: soft, non-tender, healed subcostal scar. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, co-test collected. Extremities: no edema. Skin: nothing suspicious.

A/P
- Essential hypertension - controlled. Continue HCTZ 25.
- Hereditary angioedema type 1 - on-demand icatibant; allergy yearly.
- R vestibular schwannoma after radiosurgery - surveillance MRI July.
- L C6-7 radiculopathy - quiet.
- Health maintenance: Pap/HPV today. Mammogram due in the fall. FIT kit at the next visit. Fasting labs today.
Follow up in 6 months for BP, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jen, your blood work from the physical is all normal, including kidney function, potassium and cholesterol, and your Pap and HPV test are negative, so no Pap needed for five years. Next step is a BP visit around December and the mammogram this fall. Front desk will reach out to schedule.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION (received 11/01/2023)
Date of visit: 10/30/2023
Self-referred. Copy to primary care.

HPI: 48-year-old woman with hypertension, hereditary angioedema, cervical disc disease and a prior workup for cervical radiculopathy, and a right acoustic neuroma treated with radiosurgery this year. Over the last few months she has had spells of severe headache with a pounding heartbeat and drenching sweats, coming more often and more intensely lately. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath or recent illness.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; icatibant 30 mg SC as needed. NKDA.
Family history: notable for thyroid cancer in her father. Mother with hereditary angioedema.
Social: never smoker, rare alcohol.

Exam: BP 220/110, HR 118, afebrile. Well-nourished woman, distressed with a headache during the visit. Skin moist. Fine tremor of the outstretched hands. Abdomen unremarkable.

In clinic: glucose 110, potassium 3.8, creatinine 0.9. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST or T changes.

Given the severity of the BP she was moved to our monitored treatment area and given intravenous phentolamine; BP came down to 150/90 and the headache and sweating settled. Observed for 2 hours before going home with a companion.

Assessment: paroxysms of headache, palpitations and diaphoresis with severe hypertension. Pheochromocytoma suspected.

Plan:
1. Plasma free metanephrines and 24-hour urine catecholamines sent today.
2. Avoid beta-blockers until alpha blockade is established; avoid decongestants and stimulants.
3. If biochemistry is positive, adrenal-protocol CT.
4. ED precautions for severe headache, chest pain or a sustained BP over 180.
5. Results visit in 1-2 weeks.

Endocrinology

events.reason: Results: catecholamine testing and adrenal CT

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Adrenal protocol CT of the abdomen with unenhanced, portal venous and delayed images; pelvis included on the venous phase. Status post cholecystectomy.
Left adrenal gland: 3.4 cm heterogeneous, avidly enhancing mass, attenuation 38 HU on unenhanced images. Right adrenal gland normal. Liver, spleen, pancreas and kidneys normal. No lymphadenopathy. No ascites. Pelvic organs unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 3.4 cm heterogeneous enhancing left adrenal mass; with elevated normetanephrine, consistent with pheochromocytoma.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP (received 11/14/2023)
Visit 11/08/2023

Results:
- Plasma free normetanephrine 1136 pg/mL (reference <148) - elevated
- Plasma free metanephrine 38 pg/mL (reference <57) - normal
- 24-hour urine norepinephrine 412 mcg (reference 15-80) - elevated; epinephrine 9 mcg - normal
- Adrenal CT 11/07/2023: 3.4 cm heterogeneous enhancing left adrenal mass, 38 HU unenhanced

Assessment: left adrenal pheochromocytoma, noradrenergic.

Plan:
1. Start doxazosin 2 mg at bedtime; increase to 4 mg on 11/20 and to 8 mg on 12/04 if tolerated, guided by home BP and orthostatic symptoms.
2. Liberal salt and fluid intake once alpha blockade starts.
3. Referred to endocrine surgery for laparoscopic left adrenalectomy, target early January.
4. Germline genetic testing to be sent at the post-operative visit, given the family history of thyroid cancer and as recommended for all pheochromocytoma.
5. Allergy/immunology to coordinate peri-operative C1 inhibitor prophylaxis.
Continue hydrochlorothiazide for now.

Endocrinology

ALLERGY & IMMUNOLOGY (received 12/11/2023)
Visit 12/05/2023

Seen ahead of a planned laparoscopic left adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma (January). HAE type 1, no attacks in 2023. Plan: C1 inhibitor concentrate IV within 6 hours before surgery, coordinated with anesthesia; icatibant available on the unit post-operatively. Continue on-demand icatibant at home.

reports.text:
Specimen: left adrenal gland, laparoscopic adrenalectomy.
Gross: adrenal gland with a 3.3 cm well-circumscribed tan-red nodule.
Microscopic: nested (zellballen) pattern of polygonal cells with granular cytoplasm, supported by sustentacular cells. Tumor confined to the adrenal gland. Margins negative. Adjacent adrenal cortex unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Pheochromocytoma, 3.3 cm, confined to the adrenal gland; margins negative.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: endocrine surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT (received 01/17/2024)
Date: 01/10/2024
Procedure: laparoscopic left adrenalectomy
Preop diagnosis: left adrenal pheochromocytoma, alpha-blocked on doxazosin 8 mg.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal with arterial line. C1 inhibitor concentrate given intravenously before induction per allergy/immunology for hereditary angioedema.

Lateral decubitus positioning. Four ports. The splenic flexure and spleen were mobilized, the left adrenal vein was identified and ligated early, and the gland was dissected free and removed intact in a retrieval bag. Intraoperative BP lability was managed by anesthesia with short-acting agents. EBL minimal. No complications.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: endocrine surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 01/17/2024)
Admitted 01/10/2024, discharged 01/12/2024.

Procedure: laparoscopic left adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma (pathology final 01/15: pheochromocytoma 3.3 cm, confined, margins negative).
Course: one night in step-down for BP and glucose monitoring, no hypotension requiring pressors, glucose normal. No angioedema. Diet resumed POD 1.

Medication changes: doxazosin STOPPED. Continue hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Icatibant as needed (unchanged).
Follow-up: endocrine surgery 2 weeks; endocrinology in 6-8 weeks with plasma metanephrines.

documents.title: Surgical records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Adrenalectomy records reviewed. Pathology pheochromocytoma, margins clear. Doxazosin stopped, back on HCTZ only.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY FOLLOW-UP (received 03/19/2024)
Visit 03/12/2024

Two months after laparoscopic left adrenalectomy. No spells since surgery; headaches and sweating gone. Home BP 118-128/74-82 on HCTZ alone.

Plasma free normetanephrine 96 pg/mL and metanephrine 30 pg/mL - both normal.
Germline pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma panel (RET, VHL, SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, SDHAF2, NF1, MAX, TMEM127, FH): no pathogenic variants identified.

Assessment: pheochromocytoma, resected, biochemically cured; no hereditary syndrome found.
Plan: plasma metanephrines yearly; return sooner for recurrent spells. BP management back to primary care.

Endocrinology

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received 04/28/2025)
Arrival 04/23/2025 15:10, discharged 21:20.

CC: racing heart and lightheadedness.

HPI: 50-year-old woman with hypertension, hereditary angioedema (C1 inhibitor deficiency), cervical degenerative disc disease and a pheochromocytoma removed last year. About 30 minutes before arrival, while gardening, she felt her heart start racing and became lightheaded. Her hypertension is well controlled on hydrochlorothiazide; no known heart disease. No chest pain, no syncope.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; icatibant as needed. NKDA.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 170, RR 18, SpO2 98% on room air. Lungs clear. No leg swelling.

Monitor/ECG: regular narrow-QRS tachycardia, no visible P waves.

ED course: IV access placed. Adenosine given IV: the ventricular rate slowed briefly, revealing sawtooth flutter waves, and the tachycardia then resumed. Diltiazem IV given for rate control. Spontaneous conversion to sinus rhythm at about 18:30; repeat ECG sinus rhythm 76, normal. Observed further in sinus rhythm.
Labs: CBC, BMP, magnesium and TSH normal; high-sensitivity troponin normal.

Impression: atrial flutter, converted to sinus rhythm.
Disposition: home. No new medications. Please arrange outpatient cardiology follow-up. Return for recurrent palpitations, chest pain, fainting or shortness of breath.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received 10/28/2025)
Arrival 10/19/2025 13:50. Admitted to the stroke service 18:10.

CC: dizziness, vomiting, trouble walking.

HPI: 50-year-old woman with cervical degenerative disc disease and a C6-C7 herniation previously evaluated for radiculopathy. Symptoms began about two hours before arrival right after she tipped her head back to paint a ceiling: the room spinning, two episodes of vomiting, numbness of the left side of her face, and weakness of the right arm and leg.
PMH also: hypertension, hereditary angioedema, atrial flutter (ED 04/2025), pheochromocytoma resected 2024, right vestibular schwannoma after radiosurgery.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide. NKDA.

Exam: BP 150/90, HR 85, afebrile. Light touch and pinprick reduced over the left face. Right arm and leg weaker than the left. Other cranial nerves normal.

CT head without contrast: no acute abnormality.

Impression: acute posterior circulation stroke syndrome. Stroke team consulted at the bedside. Admitted to the stroke unit for MRI and workup.

reports.text:
MRI brain without contrast with diffusion-weighted imaging, plus time-of-flight MR angiography of the head and contrast-enhanced MR angiography of the neck.
Brain: focus of restricted diffusion with corresponding FLAIR signal in the left ventral midbrain at the cerebral peduncle, consistent with acute infarct. No hemorrhage. No other acute infarct. Treated right cerebellopontine angle schwannoma, unchanged. Ventricles normal.
MRA head: normal circle of Willis, basilar and posterior cerebral arteries patent, no stenosis or occlusion.
MRA neck: carotid and vertebral arteries patent without dissection, stenosis or occlusion.
reports.conclusion: Acute left ventral midbrain (cerebral peduncle) infarct. No dissection, stenosis or large-vessel occlusion.

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. LVEF 60%. Normal right ventricle. Atria normal in size. No intracardiac thrombus. Valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation. Agitated saline study: no shunt. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal study. EF 60%, no thrombus, no shunt.

documents.title: Stroke Service Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - STROKE SERVICE (received 10/28/2025)
Admitted 10/19/2025, discharged 10/23/2025.

Principal diagnosis: Weber syndrome - acute left midbrain (cerebral peduncle) infarction.

Presentation: vertigo, vomiting, left facial numbness and right arm and leg weakness after neck extension while painting; head CT negative in the ED.

Neurology examination on the morning of 10/20: left ptosis, left pupil larger than right, limited adduction and elevation of the left eye (partial left third nerve palsy); right arm and leg weakness; decreased sensation of the left face as noted in the ED. Speech clear.

Workup:
- MRI brain: acute left ventral midbrain infarct. MRA head and neck: no dissection, stenosis or occlusion.
- TTE: EF 60%, no thrombus, no shunt.
- Telemetry: sinus rhythm throughout the stay.
- LDL 94 mg/dL. A1c normal.

Assessment: infarct of the left midbrain producing Weber syndrome. With no vessel disease or dissection and a documented episode of atrial flutter in April 2025, the mechanism is felt to be cardioembolic.

Treatment: apixaban 5 mg twice daily started on 10/21/2025. Statin not started: LDL 94 with a cardioembolic mechanism and no atherosclerotic disease.

Course: right-sided strength improving, walking with standby assistance by day 3 and independently on discharge; ptosis improving. Swallow screen passed.

Discharge medications:
- Apixaban 5 mg by mouth twice daily - NEW
- Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily - continue
- Icatibant 30 mg SC as needed - continue

Follow-up: outpatient physical therapy; stroke clinic in 6-8 weeks; cardiology; primary care in 1-2 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read the stroke admission: L midbrain infarct, Weber syndrome, felt cardioembolic from the flutter, now on apixaban. Will discuss at her next contact.

documents.title: Hospital stay
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I don't know if you got the papers but I had a small stroke last month and was in the hospital for 4 days. I'm on a blood thinner now, apixaban. Doing PT twice a week and my right leg is getting better. They told me to see you but I'm not driving yet. Can I come in once I can drive?

documents.title: RE: Hospital stay
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jen, I'm so sorry to hear this, and yes, the hospital records came last week and I've read them. I'm glad the leg is improving. Keep taking the apixaban twice a day without skipping doses and keep up with PT. A video visit is fine if driving is the issue, or we can find a time once you're back on the road. Call right away for any new weakness, numbness, trouble speaking or vision change. Front desk will reach out to schedule.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received 04/28/2026)
Arrival 04/20/2026 09:30. Admitted to medicine 14:45.

CC: severe upper abdominal pain.

HPI: 50-year-old woman with hypertension, hereditary angioedema and a prior open cholecystectomy. For 24 hours, constant, sharp pain in the epigastrium that goes through to her back and is worse lying flat. She does not drink to excess and has never been told she had gallstones.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. No other medications reported at triage. NKDA, no food allergies.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 102, temperature 37.8 C (100 F). Epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding. Bowel sounds normal. No swelling of lips, face or extremities.

Labs: WBC 12,000; hemoglobin 13.5; platelets 250,000; amylase 900 U/L (normal 30-110); lipase 850 U/L (normal 0-160); triglycerides 180; calcium 9.2; liver tests normal.

Impression: acute pancreatitis. Not alcohol related; gallbladder absent. HAE attack considered less likely given the enzyme elevation.
Plan: IV fluids and analgesia. Admit to medicine.

reports.text: Right upper quadrant ultrasound. Gallbladder surgically absent. Common bile duct 5 mm, no intraductal stone. No intrahepatic biliary dilatation. Liver normal in size and echotexture. Pancreatic head seen and unremarkable; body and tail partly obscured by bowel gas. Right kidney normal. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Post-cholecystectomy. Normal-caliber common duct without stones. Pancreas partly obscured.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY - MEDICINE (received 04/28/2026)
Admitted 04/20/2026, discharged 04/23/2026.

Principal diagnosis: acute pancreatitis, drug-induced (hydrochlorothiazide suspected).

History: hypertension; hereditary angioedema type 1; left midbrain infarct (Weber syndrome) 10/2025 on apixaban; atrial flutter 04/2025; pheochromocytoma resected 01/2024; treated right vestibular schwannoma; cervical DDD; open cholecystectomy 2021.
Medication reconciliation (pharmacy fill history and patient): hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, apixaban 5 mg twice daily, icatibant as needed. The ED triage list had recorded hydrochlorothiazide only.

Course: Admission lipase 850, amylase 900. RUQ ultrasound: no gallbladder, common duct 5 mm, no stones. No alcohol excess; triglycerides 180 and calcium 9.2 do not explain it. With other causes excluded and a thiazide as her only long-term drug besides apixaban, the pancreatitis was attributed to hydrochlorothiazide. Treated with IV fluids and analgesia; pain settled and diet advanced by day 3. Lipase 140 on 04/22. No angioedema during the stay.

Discharge medications:
- Hydrochlorothiazide - STOPPED (suspected cause of pancreatitis; avoid thiazides)
- Amlodipine 5 mg by mouth daily - NEW, for blood pressure
- Apixaban 5 mg by mouth twice daily - continue
- Icatibant 30 mg SC as needed - continue

Follow-up: primary care in 1-2 weeks for BP and medication review.
Allergies/intolerances: NKDA; hydrochlorothiazide - pancreatitis (added this admission).
